identity: Engineer and university teacher · People's Republic of China · 1911–2009
title: Qian Xuesen's birth chart
metaDescription: Qian Xuesen's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 18.0° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Mars holds a trine to Uranus at 0.5° — close enough to weld drive to disruption. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 18.0° of Sagittarius is the Sun's exact seat — second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Mars in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 8.5° Capricorn, Venus at 1.9° Scorpio, Mars at 26.6° Taurus. Mercury in a earth sign reads as thought with its feet on the ground; Venus in a water sign reads as attraction that works by atmosphere; Mars in a earth sign reads as effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mars a third of the circle apart from Uranus, 0.5° off exact. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, Jupiter sextile Uranus at 3.0°, and Mars sextile Neptune at 3.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Sun makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, three placements stand out. Venus in Scorpio at 1.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Taurus at 26.6° is in detriment; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 0.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 earth, 2 fire, 2 water, 1 air; by modality, 3 mutable, 3 cardinal, 3 fixed. Earth counts what remains: the built, the kept, the finished. Promise weighs less than delivery. Mars, Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Leo into Virgo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.1° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
